root_cause.text: `biovec_phys_mergeable()` in the block layer merged physically contiguous `bvec` segments without verifying they came from the same `dev_pagemap`, so zone device pages from different pgmap chunks could be coalesced into one bio segment and lose the correct `page_pgmap()` association.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `zone_device_pages_have_same_pgmap(vec1->bv_page, vec2->bv_page)` as an early reject in `biovec_phys_mergeable()`, and the CVE text explains that `iov_iter_extract_bvecs()` can stop at pgmap boundaries while `bio_iov_iter_get_pages()` continues filling the bio, allowing contiguous bvecs from different pgmaps to be merged incorrectly.

intent_record.intent_summary: Reject biovec merges unless both pages belong to the same zone device pgmap, fixing invalid physical mergeability decisions.
intent_record.what: In `biovec_phys_mergeable()`, a new early return was added: the function now calls `zone_device_pages_have_same_pgmap(vec1->bv_page, vec2->bv_page)` and returns `false` if the two pages do not share the same pgmap, before the existing Xen-specific and mask-based mergeability checks.
intent_record.how: This prevents two adjacent biovecs from being treated as physically mergeable when they come from different zone device memory mappings, which would otherwise allow incorrect request merging across incompatible pages.

grouping_result.intent: Reject biovec merges unless both pages belong to the same zone device pgmap, fixing invalid physical mergeability decisions.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it prevents biovec physical merges unless the pages share the same zone device pgmap, which fixes the incorrect coalescing of pages from different pgmap chunks.

candidates.rationale: This is the physical-contiguity check that allows bvec merging based only on addresses. In the vulnerable code path, mergeability was decided without any dev_pagemap/zone-device pgmap validation, so this statement is part of the overly permissive merge decision.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the physical-contiguity merge check that allowed bvecs to be merged solely based on adjacent addresses. Because it did not verify that both pages came from the same dev_pagemap, zone device pages from different pgmap chunks could be coalesced incorrectly, causing loss of the correct page_pgmap() association.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function already contains the physical-contiguity merge check and the segment-boundary check together. It computes `addr1` and `addr2`, rejects non-contiguous pages with `if (addr1 + vec1->bv_len != addr2) return false;`, and then enforces the boundary constraint with `if ((addr1 | mask) != ((addr2 + vec2->bv_len - 1) | mask)) return false;`. Since the root cause was merging physically contiguous bvecs without verifying the segment boundary / pgmap-related boundary condition, this commit’s version already includes the additional boundary guard and does not show the vulnerable construct by itself.
